recordedFailureRepaired.summary: The delivered participant guide contradicted itself about one field. participant-instructions.md said the packet wrote 'city, state and ZIP on the proposed order' and then listed that same order's State line, at section 1, under 'What the platform deliberately left blank' with 'Write your state on it yourself'.

whichSentenceWasTrue.decision: The packet DOES write the state on JDF 686's section-1 rule whenever the value held for the participant fits it. The 'deliberately left blank' bullet was the false sentence and has been removed.
controllingEvidence: reports/actual-writes.json documents[1] (canonical JDF-686) carries field defendant-state, factId participant.state, drawnText ['CO'], expected 'CO', matchesExpected true, at rect x 393.93 y 380.38 w 27.25 on the measured rule x 391.93 to 423.18, width 31.25.

production-field-map.json places JDF-686/defendant-state in JDF-686 canonicalWrites with factId participant.state, and in JDF-686 boundaryRefusals with unfittable.value 'Colorado'. The map was already correct and per-fixture; it was not the defect.
reports/blanks-left-for-the-participant.json nearMissesRefusedByRole already said 'writes the state on the form's own drawn rule'.

pdftotext -layout of the delivered canonical.pdf reads 'City: Denver  State: CO  Zip Code: 80202' on the JDF 686 page; of the delivered boundary.pdf it reads 'City: Colorado Springs  State:  Zip Code: 80921-2214'.
whichSentenceWasTrue.whyItIsConditionalRatherThanAlwaysTrue: The write is decided per packet by scripts/rcap-official-forms/rcap-text-fitting.mjs. Canonical binds participant.state='CO' and it fits; boundary binds 'Colorado' and it is refused as unfittable and left for the participant. An unconditional sentence in either direction is false for one of the two fixtures.

rows.whatWasDone: Three changes, all in scripts/build-census-v1-co_municipal_conviction_seal-set.mjs, all in generated prose. (1) Deleted the 'What the platform deliberately left blank' bullet claiming the order's State line is left blank and telling the participant to write a state on it; a comment in its place records why it may not be listed there. (2) Added narrowRuleWrittenInOneFixtureOnly(maps), which finds the one write whose rule is below the shared reader's default minimum AND which the boundary column refuses as unfittable, and emits a measured, conditional note in 'What the platform filled in, and what it did not': it names the rule's measured width, says the line is written for some participants and left for others, tells the participant to look at it, to leave a state already printed there alone, to write one only if the rule is empty, and says which key of reports/actual-writes.json answers it for the packet in hand. The note is derived from the field map, not asserted, so it disappears if the geometry or the fitting outcome ever changes. (3) Qualified the 'Written for you' sentence with 'where the value held for you fits the rule the form draws'. Also extended the nearMissesRefusedByRole finding for 'State (section 1)' so the near-miss record states the same conditional fact as the guide and the map.
whatWasDeliberatelyNotDone: No overlay geometry, no anchor, no write box and no fixture fact was touched. The bytes were already right; the guide was wrong about them.

No fee, waiting period, exclusion set, objection mechanic, service rule or notarization was added. legal-design-track-registry.json still carries rules.fees 'Unconfirmed. The fee must be confirmed before building.' and the builder still asserts on that sentence; the packet still states no amount.
No sweep across Colorado. Only this family was read or written.

measurementsThatContradictARecordInThisR.whatIsWrongWithIt: 24.3 is less than 27.25, so on its own numbers the refusal reads as a refusal of a value that fits. The refusal is in fact correct: scripts/rcap-official-forms/rcap-text-fitting.mjs compares against usableWidth = rect.width - HORIZONTAL_PADDING = 27.25 - 4 = 23.25, and 24.3 > 23.25. The comparison basis simply is not in the record.
measurementsThatContradictARecordInThisR.notedNotRepaired: The omission is in the shared module's refusal object, which is emitted by finalizeFlatOverlay and consumed by many families in other lanes. That module's own comment already names this exact gap on the North Dakota close-petition boundary fixture and exports usableWidthOf for it. Repairing it here would be a cross-lane edit outside this dispatch, so it is reported rather than changed.
